name: Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  FEBRUARY 22, 2024

1.  CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall
  Council Chamber.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Brown Schachter, Olson, Halvorsen, Martin,
  Munday, Rowe

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Persichina, Combs, Nash, Varner

  ALSO PRESENT:  Deputy Clotworthy, LACSD

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Public Works Director
  Reggie Greene, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, OCTOBER 3,
  2023.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MARTIN to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 3, 2023.

There being no objection, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

Lynn Yen, Hitching Post Drive, requested consideration of adding a leading pedestrian interval at
PVDN/PVDE for the pedestrians walking southbound across PVDN simultaneously with vehicles
turning right from PVDE onto PVDN on the green light.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST - NO RIGHT
  TURN ON RED WITH TIME RESTRICTIONS

Director Wahba stated that since the No Right Turn on Red sign was installed last year, staff has
received numerous complaints. Staff has observed that drivers are not obeying the sign; the
Deputy has stopped people but he is not aware of anyone being ticketed. Staff reached out to
interested parties and received several letters expressing their concerns with the sign. Following
his introduction, Reggie Greene provided a brief presentation.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene reiterated that several complaints have been received since
the sign was installed, the Sheriff’s have issued warning to motorists, and staff has observed
people ignoring the sign. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene summarized the timeline of the
actions taken by Council on the No Right Turn on Red sign. The following time restrictions were
proposed:

  •  7:30 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. based on counts taken as part of the
  Crossing Guard Study.
  •  7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. based on citizens recommendations.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated staff recommends that the No Turn on Red prohibition
be restricted to Monday through Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.
Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, February 22, 2024
 CHAIR SCHACHTER requested feedback/direction from the committee members.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON stated he previously resided near that intersection and made
that turn frequently. He has encountered close calls with horses and their riders. He stated that
the time restriction would help with children crossing the intersection, but there is still concern with
horses.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE shared his experience observing the intersection between 6 p.m.
and 6:30 p.m. He noted that many drivers took the red as if it was a green light and did not stop.
He reported that during the whole time, only two cars complied with stopping on red. He
proceeded to try crossing the intersection and a vehicle turning right slowed, but did not fully stop,
and came two inches from him as he stepped into the crosswalk. He recommends a light at night
on the sign since it is dark.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN stated that his son tried crossing the intersection, and no one
stopped.

Director Wahba explained why the leading pedestrian interval will not protect pedestrians from
motorists turning right and suggested that a right turn on green arrow only assuming drivers are
making a stop on a red.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene noted that the challenge they face is that drivers are used to
making a right on a red light since it is legal in California. He also stated that there is a concern
with U-turns with people who are dropping off their children at the George F Canyon Nature
Center; the U-turn would need to be restricted.

Ms. Yen explained that a leading pedestrian interval would help when crossing from the
Dapplegray arena to George F Canyon.

John Robison, Hitching Post Drive, discussed his experience with the intersection and expressed
that the No Right Turn on Red is not a good idea. He recommended push button activated in-
ground pedestrian lights. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that the in-ground pedestrian
lights cannot be used at a signalized intersection.

Paul Mollalen, Hitching Post Drive, assessed the intersection while walking with his wife and
stated there have been some close calls and stated that the issue with the intersection is beyond
the proposed hours. He also expressed his concern with additional pedestrian traffic with the
development of Founders Park and the new Community Center. He added that there are visibility
issues at that intersection with the clutter of signs. Mr. Mollalen suggested a push button activated
red arrow for motorists. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated this would require signal
modifications, but this may be a possibility and stated that he can bring this back with an update
on feasibility.

Mr. Mollalen stated that he has observed that since the sign was installed, people use the Nature
Center parking lot to cut through to get onto PVDE and expressed his concern with the new design
for the Nature Center, which allows an easier path through the parking lot onto PVDE.

Deputy Clotworthy stated that motorists were only given warnings per the desire of the city;
however, if there is direction given to the Sheriff’s, they can begin issuing citations and begin
enforcements of that intersection.

Resident Lynn Yen spoke on the schools nearby and how they are affected. She provided copies
of the school schedules to the committee and staff.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that narrowing down a time to satisfy all schedules is a
challenge and suggested an electronic signal that is activated when someone is actually crossing
the intersection.

CHAIR SCHACHTER that the sign has only been installed since November (2023). There needs
to be more time for people to be retrained and the No Turn on Red needs to be enforced. She
also expressed concern with having two time restriction blocks of time.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, February 22, 2024
 Director Wahba stated the green arrow is not recommended for that intersection. However, the
push button activated red arrow might work best for that intersection.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN asked if it is common to have a flashing yellow warning
light at a signaled intersection. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that this may not be a
possibility but will look into this. He added that there needs to be more illumination in the corners
at that intersection. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that lighting could be added to the
signal to illuminate each corner.

In response to a question by Mr. Mollanen, Director Wahba stated that the No Right Turn on Red
sign at PVDN and Rolling Hills Road was installed about fifteen years ago. Mr. Mollanen stated
that he rarely sees drivers go through that sign.

Director Wahba stated that enforcement will help with compliance of the No Turn on Red sign.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE, Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene
stated that the traffic accident report was included in the agenda for the October 3, 2023 meeting.

Deputy Clotworthy expressed concern with doing nothing at the intersection prior to it being further
developed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY expressed concern with the No Turn on Red sign at all times
remaining until another solution is found and suggested adding the time restriction.

Director Wahba stated that this will be a compromise with the community until another solution is
found.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON made a motion seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE to,

  DIRECT STAFF TO ALTER THE EXISTING SIGN BY ADDING RESTRICTIONS FROM
  7:00 A.M. TO 6:00 P.M. MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY, BELOW THAT SIGN AND
  INSTRUCT DEPUTIES TO ISSUE CITATIONS.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN requested an amended motion by having the restrictions
extended to seven days, giving consideration to children who participate in sports and other
activities on the weekends.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON amended his motion to include seven days.

AYES:  BROWN SCHACHTER, OLSON, HALVORSEN, MARTIN, MUNDAY, ROWE
NOES:
ABSENT:  PERSICHINA, COMBS, NASH, VARNER
ABSTAIN:

Direction was also given to staff to conduct further research on other options while having these
restrictions in place.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON
to,

  DIRECT STAFF TO CONDUCT FURTHER RESEARCH ON A PEDESTRIAN
  ACTIVATED RED ARROW AND IF THIS IS DONE, REMOVAL OF THE NO RIGHT
  TURN ON RED SIGN.

AYES:  BROWN SCHACHTER, OLSON, HALVORSEN, MARTIN, MUNDAY, ROWE
NOES:
ABSENT:  PERSICHINA, COMBS, NASH, VARNER
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that this recommendation will be presented to the City Council at its
meeting on March 12, 2024.

B. PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST (PVDE), NEAR HARBOR SIGHT DRIVE; SPEEDING
  CONCERNS AND SIGNAGE
Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, February 22, 2024
 Director Wahba provided a brief presentation summarizing the staff report. He stated this item
was brought forward due to a request from residents in the area. He spoke about the existing
signage and how many have missed that signage due to the speed. The sign is faded and placed
too far down. He noted there were two solar speed signs placed in a nearby area due to the same
speeding issues. Director Wahba recommends new signage or solar speed signs. The two signs
were about $20,000 including the installation.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene provided a presentation summarizing the staff report, which
included data from the 2021 Engineering and Traffic Survey. He observed that the existing sign
is faded and suggested changing the graphic to depict both intersections.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that additional traffic controls that could be considered
include:

  •  Installation of intersection head signs with flashing beacon.
  •  Installation of LED line speed limit signs.
  •  Installation of radar speed feedback signs.

Traffic Engineering Deputy stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety Committee
discuss the concerns with speeds on PVDE, receive public testimony, and provide direction to
staff regarding the matter; it is further recommended that the faded T-intersection sign be replaced
with a sign that depicts the actual geometry of the roadway. Should the committee wish to explore
the options presented, staff will provide location and costs at the next meeting.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN stated that living near Chandler Ranch Road, he is more
conscientious of the new radar speed signs. This has been helpful for himself and others.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON stated that his wife was involved in an accident in that area, he
also expressed the dangerous speeds observed in that intersection. He suggested additional
signage to slow down, especially when there is a school bus that picks-up and drops-off at that
intersection.

CHAIR SCHACHTER inquired whether there was any research done in that area or other similar
research that would apply to this intersection.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated there is research but he is unaware of what it states.
He commented that habits are changed when the signs initially go up and then residents may
become complacent.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY recommended replacing the existing signage and see if that
works prior to investing in a more expensive sign.

Director Wahba suggested relocating the sign and adding a “Slow Curve Ahead” sign. Traffic
Engineering Deputy Greene stated that he can look into moving it further south.

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN expressed concern with the blind turn going up to Rancho
Palos Verdes; moving the sign closer to that and adding a secondary sign would be helpful.

CHAIR SCHACHTER recommended a flashing yellow light to alert drivers that there is a stop sign
ahead.

Deputy Clotworthy stated that the radar signs are great and, in his experience, they are helpful
for slowing people down.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked if there is a first step prior to the proposed options.

Director Wahba suggested replacing the existing sign and adding a” Slow Curve Ahead” sign.
These two signs would be approximately $1,000.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE, Director Wahba stated that the
current speed limit sign for this road is on the right going up the hill. He added that there have
been new signs installed on PVDE to remind drivers more often about the speed limit.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  4
Minutes, February 22, 2024
 In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE, Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene
provided clarification on the presentation slide that listed verbiage on the 10 miles per hour pace
speed.

COMMISSIONER OLSON inquired if the speed limit be changed to 35 mph. Traffic Engineering
Deputy Greene explained that this would be in violation of the California Vehicle Code.

Deputy Clotworthy explained the importance of maintaining a speed survey in the city.

A brief discussion ensued on a secondary sign.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene will bring back more information on a secondary sign.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE made a motion to,

  INCLUDE A YELLOW FLASHING LIGHT WITH THE REPLACEMENT OF THE
  INTERSECTION SIGN.

A discussion ensued on the yellow flashing beacon and sign options.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY, Director Wahba stated that this
request came from the Homeowners Association.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN expressed the dangers of speed in that area.

COMMITTEE MEMBER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY
to,
  RECOMMEND TO THE CITY COUNCIL REPLACEMENT OF THE EXISTING SIGN AND
  RELOCATION PER STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION AND RE-EVALUATE THE
  INTERSECTION IN THE FUTURE.

AYES:  BROWN SCHACHTER, OLSON, HALVORSEN, MARTIN, MUNDAY, ROWE.
NOES:
ABSENT:  PERSICHINA, COMBS, NASH, VARNER.
ABSTAIN:

Director Wahba stated that this recommendation will be presented to the City Council at its
meeting on March 12, 2024.

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

A. PARKING IN FRONT OF RED CURB AT 627 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE

Director Wahba provided background on the issues regarding parking in front of 627 Deep Valley
Drive and people parking across the street at the library. He stated that they will look into the
crosswalk as part of the HSIP grant along with the repaving of Deep Valley Drive. He noted a lot
of parents park in front of the red curb which is also located in front of a fire hydrant. He also
stated that parents are typically waiting in the vehicle in front of red curb and cannot be cited per
the California Vehicle code. Therefore, residents are recommending adding a “No Stopping” or
“No Waiting” sign in front of curb.

Deputy Clotworthy stated that he will look into getting clarification on this.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY expressed his concern with the insufficient parking in this area.
He stated that enforcement may be problematic if there is not a solution in place first.

Director Wahba stated that the Task Order for this project will be presented to the City Council at
its March 12, 2024 meeting.

Director Wahba requested that Deputy Clotworthy inquire whether enforcement is an option and
suggested issuing warnings prior to citations.

B. TRAFFIC SIGNAL TIMING ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  5
Minutes, February 22, 2024
 Director Wahba noted this item was requested by a committee member who is not present. He
stated that the traffic on PVDN, signal timing, and the project at London Lane (Dapplegray School)
and PVDN to make intersection improvements will be presented to the City Council in either March
or April.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY distributed a document, which shows the traffic congestion on
PVDN. He suggested that drivers coming from Dapplegray School onto PVDN as well as those
coming from Rolling Hills Road, trigger a red light and these cars should wait longer since they
impact hundreds of cars on PVDN.

A discussion ensued on this issue.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MARTIN to,

  DIRECT STAFF TO WORK WITH WILLDAN TO CONDUCT ANOTHER TRAFFIC
  SIGNAL TIMING ANALYSIS ON PVDN

AYES:  BROWN SCHACHTER, OLSON, HALVORSEN, MARTIN, MUNDAY, ROWE
NOES:
ABSENT:  PERSICHINA, COMBS, NASH, VARNER
ABSTAIN:

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER HALVORSEN expressed his concerns of speeding vehicles when
making the left-hand turn from Chandler Ranch Rd. going northbound on Palos Verdes East.
Director Wahba stated that there have been modifications made to the intersection to improve
visibility, and the installation of the new solar-powered signs; the last solution would be adding a
traffic signal.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that pedestrians crossing Silver Spur Road and PVDN
have expressed concern with motorists going through the intersection. She asked Deputy
Clotworthy to forward this information to the traffic deputy.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting at 8:17 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved by,

______________________________  _______________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Pam Brown Schachter, Chair
